method: Every dated promise a developer made about a project (handover, construction start, structure, other milestones, permits, rental programme) is read by claude-haiku-5-5 from two stores the research agent already keeps: the research record of each project and the copy of the developer or listing page on every day the agent read it. Each item must carry an exact quote: software checks the quote word for word against the stored text and checks that it contains the year, and rejects it otherwise. A promise is kept when the event is shown done no later than the promised date; broken only when the date has passed and an observation made after that date shows it had not happened (for handover: the project is still not completed in our research record); moved when the same source later shows a later date (an earlier copy of the same page, or a research record that states the original date), with how many times and by how many months; pending when the date is still ahead; unknown when the date has passed and we hold no dated evidence either way, or the event happened but we cannot show it was on time. When the newest copy states two dates for the same promise, claude-sonnet-5-5 decides which is current. Projects are anonymous: quotes are not published (they would identify the project); each promise carries the first 16 hex characters of the SHA-256 of its quote and, for page copies, of the page text, which is the fingerprint already sealed in the daily log.

statuses.kept: done no later than the promised date
statuses.broken: date passed, and a later observation shows it had not happened
statuses.moved: date pushed later at least once, new date still ahead
statuses.unknown: date passed with no dated evidence either way, or done but timing not shown

spend.note: Computed from token usage at list prices: 0.10 / 0.50 USD (haiku) and 2 / 10 USD (sonnet) per million tokens in / out. The first run (4 Nov 2026 08:38 UTC, logged as 0.26 USD) used a 10 times higher estimate.
